## Natural history notes

A small native perennial herb in the spurge family, characterized by slender branching stems, narrow leaves, and tiny greenish flowers typical of Euphorbia. Lesser Florida Spurge occurs in dry, open habitats of southern Florida, including pine rocklands, scrubby flatwoods, and other sandy or rocky uplands. It is adapted to full sun, nutrient-poor soils, and periodically disturbed or fire-maintained vegetation communities. The species is native to Florida and is particularly associated with the southern peninsula, where it can occur locally in relatively undisturbed pineland habitats.
